title: Insights into Serotonin-Receptor Binding and Stability via Molecular Dynamics Simulations: Key Residues for Electrostatic Interactions and Signal Transduction
one_liner_zh: 该文通过分子动力学模拟研究血清素与G蛋白偶联受体的结合稳定性与信号转导，属于蛋白-小分子配体互作，非蛋白质-DNA互作体系，且方法虽为MD但对象与本课题无关。
abstract: Serotonin-receptor binding plays a key role in several neurological and biological processes, including mood, sleep, hunger, cognition, learning, and memory. In this article, we performed molecular dynamics simulation to examine the key residues that play an essential role in the binding of serotonin to the G-protein-coupled 5-HT$_{1B}$ receptor (5HT$_{1B}$R) via electrostatic interactions. Key residues for electrostatic interactions were identified via bond distance analysis and frustration analysis method. An end-point free energy calculation method determines the stability of the 5-HT$_{1B}$R due to serotonin binding. The single-point mutation of the polar/charged amino acid residues (Asp129, Thr134) on the binding sites and the calculation of binding free energy validates the quantitative contribution of these residues in the stability of the serotonin-receptor complex. The principal component analysis reflects that the serotonin-bound 5-HT$_{1B}$R is more stabilized than the apo-receptor regarding dynamical changes. The difference dynamic cross-correlations map shows the correlation between the transmembranes and mini-G$_{o}$, which indicates that the signal transduction happens between mini-G$_{o}$ and the receptor. Allosteric pathway analysis reveals the key nodes for signal transduction in 5-HT$_{1B}$R. These results provide useful insights into the study of signal transduction pathways and mutagenesis to regulate the functionality of the complex. The developed protocols can be applied to study local non-covalent interactions and long-range allosteric communications in any protein-ligand system for computer-aided drug design.
abstract_zh: 血清素受体结合在多种神经和生物过程中发挥关键作用，包括情绪、睡眠、饥饿、认知、学习和记忆。本文中，我们进行了分子动力学 (molecular dynamics) 模拟，以检查通过静电相互作用在血清素与G蛋白偶联的5-HT$_{1B}$受体 (5HT$_{1B}$R) 结合中起关键作用的关键残基。通过键距分析和挫折分析方法识别了静电相互作用的关键残基。一种端点自由能计算方法确定了血清素结合对5-HT$_{1B}$R稳定性的影响。对结合位点上极性/带电氨基酸残基（Asp129、Thr134）进行单点突变，并通过结合自由能计算验证了这些残基在血清素-受体复合物稳定性中的定量贡献。主成分分析反映，在动力学变化方面，血清素结合的5-HT$_{1B}$R比脱辅基受体更稳定。差异动态交叉相关图显示了跨膜区与mini-G$_{o}$之间的相关性，表明信号转导发生在mini-G$_{o}$与受体之间。变构通路分析揭示了5-HT$_{1B}$R中信号转导的关键节点。这些结果为研究信号转导通路和突变调控复合物功能提供了有用的见解。所开发的方案可应用于研究任何蛋白质-配体系统中的局部非共价相互作用和长程变构通讯，以用于计算机辅助药物设计。
